question: Should ClawHub sign the existing stored hosted-feed publication, or approve a new versioned signed feed contract for OpenClaw clients?
rationale: Feed signing changes the client trust boundary and production secret contract, while current specs explicitly keep signing behind a separate key-management and trust-root decision.

options.title: Sign Stored Publications
options.body: Require the signer to wrap the current `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact integrity semantics, and document public-key rollout before merge.

options.title: Approve A New Signed Contract
options.body: Accept a new versioned schema only after the matching OpenClaw parser, public route, key distribution, and compatibility behavior are documented.

options.title: Pause Signing
options.body: Keep the draft parked until signing keys, trust roots, route ownership, and client support can land together.

recommendation.title: Sign Stored Publications
recommendation.body: Require the signer to wrap the current `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact integrity semantics, and document public-key rollout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the hosted-feed contract and stored-publication boundary that this PR changes.
